newsitem.title: USA: Ind. Treasurer files legal challenge to arena law.
newsitem.headline: Ind. Treasurer files legal challenge to arena law.

text.p: Indiana Treasurer Joyce Brinkman said Wednesday she has filed a state lawsuit challenging the constitutionality of a law providing part of the financing for a new downtown Indianapolis basketball arena.

Brinkman said she does not oppose the Indiana Pacers arena, but filed the lawsuit Tuesday in Marion County Superior Court because she believes the legislation violated protections against multiple subject matters and special legislation.
Indiana lawmakers last month approved the law creating a professional sports development district in Indianapolis for financing the partly bond-financed $175 million arena.

The Indianapolis City-County council voted Monday night to approve the district, which will capture up to $5 million of sales and income tax revenues annually to back $50 million of bonds for the arena.
The law enabling the professional sports district also included provisions for annexation in northern Indiana and creation of a bond bank for Lawrenceburg in southeastern Indiana, Brinkman said.
The lawsuit assigned to Judge Cynthia Ayers had not yet been scheduled for a court date on Wednesday, a court clerk said.

Public financing plans for the arena also include a $4.7 million infrastructure grant, $9.3 million of restricted reserves from the Capital Improvement Board and $7 million in revenues from the Circle Centre Mall designated for downtown development.

Financing for the arena scheduled to open in fall 1999 includes $57 million from the Pacers owners and $37 million of bonds backed by Circle Centre Mall investors who have committed $3.7 million of annual revenues for debt service.
Eli Lilly & Co has pledged the use of land adjacent to the arena site valued at $10 million for parking and construction staging as well.
